title: EU Payments Regulation: PSD2, PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation (EU Edition)
summary: An eight-module programme on EU payments regulation for supervisors and firms, covering PSD2 and EMD2 today and the PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation reform package.
intro: This training programme equips supervisors and payment firms to apply the current EU payments framework and prepare for the PSD3 and PSR reform: authorisation, safeguarding, strong customer authentication, fraud liability, open banking, access to payment systems and supervision.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give supervisors and practitioners a clear map of EU payments regulation as it stands under PSD2 and the Second E-Money Directive, and of the changes brought by the PSD3 and Payment Services Regulation reform package. Participants leave able to assess authorisation, safeguarding, fraud and access arrangements against both regimes and to plan a structured transition.
sections.What It Covers: The PSD2 and EMD2 framework and its lessons, the PSD3 and PSR reform package, authorisation and the integration of e-money into payment services, safeguarding and wind-down, strong customer authentication, fraud and liability including impersonation fraud and payee verification, open banking and access to data, access to payment systems and bank accounts, instant payments and e-money tokens, and supervision and enforcement.
Intended Audience: Authorisation, supervision and policy staff at national competent authorities covering payment and e-money institutions
Compliance, risk, legal, fraud and product staff at payment institutions, e-money institutions and banks
Senior managers and directors of payment firms responsible for regulatory change and transition planning
Learning Objectives: Explain the current PSD2 and EMD2 framework and the main elements of the PSD3 and PSR reform package
Apply authorisation, capital and safeguarding requirements, including the integration of e-money into the payments regime
Assess strong customer authentication, fraud prevention and liability arrangements, including payee verification
Evaluate open banking interfaces and the rules on access to data, payment systems and bank accounts
Explain the interplay with instant payments, MiCA e-money tokens and the AML/CFT framework
Design a supervisory approach or firm transition plan for the reformed regime
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module combines a technical briefing with case studies, red-flag exercises and change-mapping work, and modules can be selected or tailored for supervisors, payment institutions, e-money institutions or banks.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of payment services, e-money or their supervision is helpful. No legal background or prior knowledge of EU law is required.
Core Reading: Directive (EU) 2015/2366 on payment services in the internal market (PSD2)
Directive 2009/110/EC on the taking up, pursuit and prudential supervision of the business of electronic money institutions (Second E-Money Directive)
Regulation (EU) 2024/886 amending Regulations (EU) No 260/2012 and (EU) 2021/1230 and Directives 98/26/EC and (EU) 2015/2366 as regards instant credit transfers in euro (Instant Payments Regulation)
CPMI, Fast Payments: Enhancing the Speed and Availability of Retail Payments (2016)

modules.title: The EU Payments Framework and the Reform Package
modules.summary: How PSD2 and EMD2 shaped EU payments, what the review found, and how the reform splits the framework between PSD3 for licensing and supervision and a directly applicable Payment Services Regulation for conduct rules.
objectives: Explain the scope, structure and achievements of PSD2 and EMD2
Identify the weaknesses the review found in fraud, open banking, enforcement and the level playing field
Map the PSD3 and PSR reform package and its legislative and transition stages
syllabus: Payment services, e-money and exclusions: the current perimeter
Lessons from PSD2: fraud, interface quality, divergent application and arbitrage
PSD3 for licensing and supervision, the PSR for conduct and operational rules
EBA technical standards, guidelines and Q&As under both regimes

modules.title: Authorisation, Capital and the Integration of E-Money
modules.summary: Authorising payment and e-money institutions today, how the reform folds e-money institutions into a single payment institution category, and the reauthorisation, capital and governance implications for existing firms.
objectives: Assess applications against authorisation, capital and fitness requirements
Explain how e-money issuance becomes a payment service under the reform
Plan for reauthorisation and transitional arrangements for existing licence holders
syllabus: Programme of operations, business plan, governance and own funds methods
A single payment institution category with e-money services
Reauthorisation, transitional periods and grandfathering questions
Agents, distributors, passporting and the narrowing of exclusions

modules.title: Safeguarding, Wind-Down and Prudential Resilience
modules.summary: How safeguarding protects user funds under PSD2 and EMD2, the changes proposed in the reform, and how supervisors and firms test safeguarding, reconciliation and wind-down readiness.
objectives: Apply segregation, insurance and guarantee safeguarding methods correctly
Assess reconciliation, concentration risk and safeguarding audits
Evaluate wind-down plans and the return of funds on failure
syllabus: Relevant funds, timing, safeguarding accounts and secure low-risk assets
Reform changes: concentration risk and safeguarding with central banks
Daily reconciliation, shortfalls and safeguarding audits
Case study: safeguarding failures revealed on insolvency

modules.title: Strong Customer Authentication and Operational Risk
modules.summary: The SCA regime and its exemptions, how the reform clarifies scope, accessibility and responsibilities, and the operational and security risk requirements that now sit alongside DORA.
objectives: Apply SCA requirements, exemptions and transaction risk analysis
Explain reform changes to SCA scope, accessibility and outsourcing of authentication
Assess the interaction between payment security rules and DORA
syllabus: SCA elements, dynamic linking and the main exemptions
Merchant-initiated and mail and telephone order transactions
Accessibility for persons with disabilities and customers without smartphones
Payment security rules, DORA incident reporting and technical service providers

modules.title: Fraud, Liability and Impersonation Scams
modules.summary: The shift from unauthorised fraud to authorised push payment scams, the reform's liability rules including impersonation of payment service provider staff, payee verification and fraud data sharing, and how fraud controls are assessed.
objectives: Distinguish unauthorised transactions, authorised push payment fraud and impersonation fraud
Apply liability, refund and gross negligence rules under the current and reformed regimes
Assess transaction monitoring, payee verification and fraud data sharing
syllabus: Unauthorised transactions, gross negligence and refund timelines
IBAN and name verification under the Instant Payments Regulation and the reform
Impersonation fraud refunds and cooperation with electronic communications providers
Fraud monitoring, data sharing, spending limits and customer education

modules.title: Open Banking and Access to Data
modules.summary: Account information and payment initiation services under PSD2, the reform's improvements to dedicated interfaces, permission dashboards and prohibited obstacles, and the wider move towards open finance.
objectives: Explain the rights and obligations of account servicing providers and third-party providers
Assess dedicated interface performance, fallback arrangements and prohibited obstacles
Evaluate customer permissions, data use and liability between providers
syllabus: Account information and payment initiation services: rights and conditions
Dedicated interfaces, performance requirements and fallback mechanisms
Permission dashboards, consent and interaction with data protection rules
From open banking to open finance: emerging proposals

modules.title: Access to Payment Systems, Accounts and New Payment Rails
modules.summary: Non-bank access to payment systems and bank accounts, instant payments, and the interplay between payments rules and MiCA e-money tokens, including dual-licensing questions for crypto-asset service providers.
objectives: Explain non-bank access to payment systems and objective, non-discriminatory account access
Assess the implications of instant payments for liquidity, fraud and sanctions screening
Analyse the interplay between e-money tokens, crypto-asset services and payment services
syllabus: Payment and e-money institution access to settlement finality systems
Bank account access, refusals, reasons and de-risking
Instant payments: availability, pricing, sanctions screening and payee verification
E-money tokens under MiCA and the payment services boundary

modules.title: Supervising Payments and Preparing for Transition
modules.summary: Risk-based supervision and enforcement of payment firms under the current and reformed regimes, including stronger powers, data and EBA convergence work, ending with a transition planning workshop for supervisors or firms.
objectives: Design risk-based supervision of payment and e-money institutions
Apply supervisory, enforcement and cross-border cooperation tools, including for agents and passporting firms
Plan the transition to PSD3 and the PSR
syllabus: Risk indicators: growth, complaints, fraud data, safeguarding and partner withdrawal
Home–host cooperation, passporting and EBA convergence work
Enforcement powers, penalties and the reform's more harmonised sanctions
Workshop: a PSD3 and PSR transition roadmap

related.title: Digital Operational Resilience under DORA (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on DORA for supervisors and financial entities: ICT risk management, incident reporting, resilience testing and TLPT, ICT third-party risk and critical provider oversight.

related.title: The EU AI Act and Financial Services (EU Edition)
related.summary: An eight-module programme on the EU AI Act for supervisors and financial firms: risk classification, high-risk credit and insurance uses, provider and deployer duties, supervision and compliance programmes.

related.title: EU Asset Management and Investment Fund Regulation (EU Edition)
related.summary: A ten-module programme mapping EU fund and asset management regulation, from UCITS, AIFMD and MiFID II to liquidity, delegation, cross-border marketing, SFDR and DORA.

related.title: Payment Services Supervision
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors to authorise and supervise payment and e-money institutions, from safeguarding and fraud to open banking, instant payments and wind-down.

related.title: Payments and E-Money Compliance
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving payment and e-money firms the practical tools to meet safeguarding, fraud, financial crime and resilience expectations.

related.title: Big Tech, Embedded Finance and Open Finance
related.summary: An eight-module programme equipping supervisors to assess big tech, embedded finance and open finance models, and their concentration, conduct and operational risks.
